accepted.name: population_by_country_unpivoted
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  country AS country,
  country_code AS country_code,
  CAST(REGEXP_REPLACE(year_name, r'^year_', '') AS INT64) AS year,
  population AS population
FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_global_population.population_by_country`,
UNNEST([
  STRUCT('year_1960' AS year_name, year_1960 AS population),
  STRUCT('year_1961', year_1961),
  STRUCT('year_1962', year_1962),
  STRUCT('year_1963', year_1963),
  STRUCT('year_1964', year_1964),
  STRUCT('year_1965', year_1965),
  STRUCT('year_1966', year_1966),
  STRUCT('year_1967', year_1967),

  STRUCT('year_2004', year_2004),
  STRUCT('year_2005', year_2005),

accepted.description: Unpivots the wide population_by_country table into one row per country-year with population value. Use this to analyze population time series, join to other year-based indicators, or compute growth rates. | Use for: time series population trends; joining population to other year-based indicators; growth rate / year-over-year population change; compare population across countries for a given year

accepted.name: health_nutrition_population_latest_by_country_indicator
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_name AS country_name,
  country_code AS country_code,
  indicator_name AS indicator_name,
  indicator_code AS indicator_code,
  value AS value,
  year AS year,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY country_code, indicator_code ORDER BY year DESC NULLS LAST) AS year_rank
FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.health_nutrition_population`
grain: one row per original observation (augmented with rank) — partitioned by country_code + indicator_code
accepted.description: Per (country_code, indicator_code) returns the most recent observation (highest year) with its value and a rank. Use to get latest available indicator values or to filter to top-K most recent by year. | Use for: retrieve latest indicator value per country; trend analysis using latest-available datapoints; filter to most recent N observations per indicator/country

accepted.name: indicator_series_catalog
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.series_code AS series_code,
  s.topic AS topic,
  s.indicator_name AS indicator_name,
  s.short_definition AS short_definition,
  s.long_definition AS long_definition,
  s.unit_of_measure AS unit_of_measure,
  s.periodicity AS periodicity,
  s.source AS source,
  csd.country_code AS country_code,
  csd.description AS country_series_description,
  st.year AS year,
  st.description AS year_description
FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.series_summary` AS s
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.country_series_definitions` AS csd
  ON s.series_code = csd.series_code
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.series_times` AS st
  ON s.series_code = st.series_code
grain: one row per series_code x country_code x year (when series_times has multiple year rows)
accepted.description: Denormalized catalog of indicator metadata by joining series_summary to country_series_definitions and series_times. One row per series_code with descriptive fields and available time descriptions. Use to enrich indicator codes with human-readable definitions and available years. | Use for: lookup indicator metadata for code; join metadata to fact tables for labeling; list available years/descriptions for a series

accepted.name: wdi_indicators_data_clean
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_name AS country_name,
  country_code AS country_code,
  indicator_name AS indicator_name,
  indicator_code AS indicator_code,
  SAFE_CAST(value AS FLOAT64) AS value,
  SAFE_CAST(year AS INT64) AS year,
  IF(value IS NULL, TRUE, FALSE) AS value_is_null
FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_wdi.indicators_data`
grain: one row per original indicators_data observation
accepted.description: Cleans and normalizes the WDI indicators_data table: preserves core columns, casts value/year to consistent types and exposes a flag for missing values. Use as a canonical fact table for WDI indicators. | Use for: time series queries on WDI indicators; joining WDI data to other series by country/year; filtering or imputing missing indicator values
